question.text: The diameter of a spherical bob is measured using a vernier callipers. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> divisions of the main scale, in the vernier callipers, are equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions of vernier scale. One main scale division is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The main scale reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>8</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale was found to coincide exactly with one of the main scale division. If the given vernier callipers has positive zero error of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>04</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the radius of the bob is _____________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
9 MSD=10 VSD
1 VSD=0.9 mm
1 MSD=1 mm
∴ L.C.=MSD-VSDMSD=1-0.91=0.1
Reading = Main scale reading + L.C. × vernier scale reading
=10+0.1×8
=10.8 mm

Reading of diameter=10.8 mm-0.4 mm=10.4 mm
radius of the bob=5.2 mm
=0.52 cm=52×10-2 cm
